title: Inversion page: how to cause a compliance failure with a fast decision model
description: A page applying Charlie Munger's inversion: deployment patterns that would reliably create violations (e.g. using the verdict as the decision, one model for every firm, gating on the cue, unpinned versions, no outcome check), each tied to a measured result and paired with the inverse practice.

comments.author: home
comments.text:
Feature: Inversion page
  Scenario: Each failure pattern is grounded
    Given the inversion page
    Then each failure pattern names the regulated decision, links to a measured result that shows it, and states the inverse practice
  Scenario: Deep links reach it
    Given any risk panel
    Then it links to the matching failure pattern on the inversion page by a stable anchor

comments.author: home
comments.text: Implemented in 8dfdccd: /how-to-fail/ with 11 recipes, anchor = recipe id (e.g. /how-to-fail/#gate-on-the-cue). Munger attribution verified at fs.blog transcript (Harvard School, 13 June 1986, quoting Jacobi).

comments.author: home
comments.text: Rewriting the inversion page as a compact Munger-style thought experiment: fast decision models can be useful, so ask what deployment choices would make them fail; preserve measured-result links and stable anchors while removing repeated detail.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Completed in 784d4df: reduced the page to a Munger inversion framing, compact failure-mode cards, concise safer alternatives, and direct evidence links. Verified with the site build and compliance tests.

right_now_summary: The inversion page links each failure pattern to measured results, inverse practices, and stable anchors from risk
